reading.body:
Digital Realty ACC4 is a 347,500 square foot building in Ashburn, Virginia with 2N+2 cooling redundancy, meaning four independent cooling paths serve the facility. The operator has not published its power capacity, so its actual IT load cannot be determined from available sources. Ashburn is part of Data Center Alley, where Digital Realty operates at least six named facilities across Northern Virginia, forming one of the largest colocation campus concentrations in the region.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which only 23 publish power capacity figures totaling 1,375 megawatts. ACC4 does not appear in the 23 published-capacity facilities, placing it outside the ranked set. Without a published power figure, this site cannot be assessed against the state's grid constraint or compared to other Virginia campuses by workload density.

The facility's specifications indicate it is designed for high-availability colocation, but absence of published capacity limits its visibility in tracking AI infrastructure scaling. Operators in Ashburn frequently omit power figures from public spec pages despite publishing them to financial audiences, making ACC4 representative of a gap between mapped physical footprint and measurable grid demand in Northern Virginia.
